newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Ringgit largely unmoved by Bank Negara remarks.
newsitem.headline: Ringgit largely unmoved by Bank Negara remarks.

text.p: The ringgit barely moved against the dollar despite warning by Bank Negara that it would not hesitate to introduce measures to curb speculative activities, dealers said.
Central bank Governor Ahmad Mohamed Don also said that Bank Negara had no choice but to allow interest rates to go up again.
"Surprisingly the ringgit did not move much after the news. We had expected Bank Negara to come out with other actions apart from its intervention," said a dealer with a large Malaysian bank.
But the dollar will be pressured by the news, he said.
The ringgit fell to 2.5020 to a dollar from around 2.5050 after the news hit the market, dealers said.
They expected dollar/ringgit to trade between 2.4950 and 2.5050 in the immediate term.
Some dealers said the central bank's warning was necessary as speculators were waiting to hit the ringgit.
Bank Negara was said to have intervened strongly in the market on Tuesday, spending an estimated $1.0 billion to help the ringgit.
The central bank again sold the dollar early on Wednesday, which sent dollar/ringgit down to a low of 2.4950, the ringgit's highest level since May 20.
Ahmad confirmed intervention by Bank Negara to defend the ringgit, but declined to give the amount of its dollar sales.
He said the central bank had sufficient reserves to meet such intervention.
